artifacts.layman_summary: Tests whether nudging a small code model's internal activations makes it invent more varied, still-correct path-search algorithms than raising temperature or prompting does; it does not.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_3
artifacts.summary: INFLUENCE ARM, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, one HF engine for every condition (per-sample seeded inverse-CDF sampler, code-block stop, 768 max tokens). Tasks: T1 open path search, T3 weighted shortest path. Correctness = sandboxed oracle on 50 fixed graphs (all must pass); idea label = AST classifier (audited vs blind gpt-4.1-mini judge on 200 programs: agreement 0.715, kappa 0.68). Baseline T=0.7 n=300: T1 BFS 205/DFS 80 (pass 0.70), T3 Dijkstra 225/BFS-relax 71 (pass 0.37); menus T1={bfs,dfs}, T3={dijkstra,bfs}. Probes at gen1..8 are at chance (boilerplate opening; algorithm name first appears at median token 23.5/46.5), so fallback F4 was used: probe on mean(gen1..32) (bal acc ~0.65-0.69 vs shuffled 0.42), hook window prompt-final+gen1..64, band layers 29-31. Sweep n=150/setting (controls 75): H-probe/H-dim (5 calibrated alphas), A3 rank-1 projection + LEACE, A4 cross-task unusualness direction, matched-norm random controls, temperature 1.0-2.0, top-k, 'new'/'novel2000' prompts, ban-top-3, generate-then-select; held-out re-draw (seeds 1000..1099) for selected settings. RESULT: no internal knob survives the pre-registered rules -> 'prompting ceiling'. Pooled pass/idea-entropy: baseline 0.53/1.05; ban-top-3 0.43/1.59 (best eligible, tops entropy front); gen-then-select 0.26/2.56; best H-dim 0.57/1.06 (held-out entropy ratio vs best temperature 0.93 T1, 1.20 T3; needed >=2; CI vs random direction includes 0); H-probe has no setting at matched pass rate; A4 dial not monotone (Spearman 0.49 T1, -0.26 T3) although its readout transfers (AUROC 1.0); judge-confirmed novel-and-correct share = 0 in every condition (all 70 rule-'other' passing programs were known algorithms), so A3 fails despite LEACE erasing idea decodability offline (T3 0.88->0.35). Mechanistic finding: H directions SELECT rather than flatten (H-dim a=0.224 turns T1 into DFS 145/150 at unchanged pass 0.68) - internal knobs give controllable choice among known ideas, not novelty; random matched-norm directions raise entropy about as much as targeted knobs. Noise floor: batch-composition re-run flips 11-17% of labels. Independent re-derivation (verify_headline.py: own oracle runner 147/147 agreement, coarse classifier 97%, pandas recomputation) reproduces headline numbers; placebo CIs include 0. Files: method_out.json (exp_gen_sol_out, 300 examples, all metrics in metadata), results/results.json (survival, CIs, Pareto, manipulation checks), figs/, gens/, scored/, judge/; vectors/ (vectors.pt + leace_T1/T3.pt) published; acts/ (split into <100 MB parts, src/acts_io.py) and caps/ kept on the run volume only.
artifacts.title: Can internal knobs beat temperature for novel code?

hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: The next iteration answers the temperature (a)/(b)/(c) questions with top-k, context seeding, 'always BFS?', mode vs average answer, the effect of prompt instructions, the BFS/DFS/Dijkstra internals and the manifold with the top-5-ban edge-vs-opposite test, and whether an internal knob reaches unusual correct ideas.
key_changes: Fixed the prompt confound: every core test now uses the user's BARE prompt, which gives a 4-5 idea menu (T1 BFS 60/DFS 15/A* 13/Dijkstra 7). All iteration-1 influence-arm conclusions are marked conditional on the output-contract prompt, which produced a two-idea menu (BFS/DFS; Dijkstra/BFS-relax) and made 'flatten vs select' untestable.

Dropped the claim that flattening the utility vector at the commitment token is the creativity knob. It failed the pre-registered rules: held-out entropy ratio 0.93/1.20 against 2 required, with the CI against a random direction including 0. Also dropped menu erasure (LEACE removed decodability but not the behaviour) and the single unusualness dial (Spearman 0.49/-0.26). Each gets one sentence in the paper.

Kept the iteration-1 LEAD (internal directions SELECT: DFS 145/150 at unchanged pass 0.68) and deepened it. It is retested on menus of 4+ ideas, where the prediction is that steering lands on the geometric neighbour, with >=5 random draws x n=150 per strength and entropy compared against the draw-averaged random entropy, as the reviewer required.

Recast bans from a choice-set restriction (nested logit over a fixed menu) to a DISPLACEMENT of the prompt-position idea state. This adds a regularity-violation test: an unbanned idea losing share, which the unreported ban-arm screen already shows (T2 ban Insertion: Bubble 43->1 vs placebo; ban Quick: Bubble 43->15; T1 ban DFS: Dijkstra 11->0). It also adds a causal Delta_h transplant/subtraction test against random displacements.

Made 'edge vs opposite side' a predicted SIGN rather than a binary hypothesis. Path search shows neighbour attraction (ban BFS->DFS 66; ban Dijkstra->A* 34; ban rare SPFA primes Dijkstra 11->50; T3 ban Dijkstra->Bellman-Ford 55; top-3 ban->IDDFS 42, the blend of the banned pair). Sorting shows family suppression (top-5 ban->Counting 45/Heap 26). Internal geometry must predict which happens.

Added the obvious alternative explanation as a baseline: an EXTERNAL text-embedding similarity of algorithm names must be beaten, or tied and reported, alongside IIA renormalisation of the placebo distribution (not the raw baseline, because the placebo sentence alone shifts T1 A* 13%->1% and T2 Bubble 60%->43%).

Recorded the actual state of the temperature arm (raw_grid.jsonl 3,623 gens; raw_seeds.jsonl 360; 51% truncated at 768 tokens; vLLM bit-reproducibility 2/20). Labelling them, with Arrhenius fits and Hill-number alpha/beta partitions, is now priority A at near-zero GPU cost. This answers the user's (a)/(b)/(c) and the seeding question.

Withdrew 'bans are mostly ignored by this 3B model'. Non-compliance is 87-95% under the contract prompt with list wording, and 0-46% under the bare prompt with short-list wording (61% on the T3 top-5 list). The wording and the contract are confounded. Question 7 is reopened as 'partially answered behaviourally'.

Imposed screening discipline. Existing ban-arm and influence-arm data are the SCREEN. CONFIRMATION is never-generated bans (rank-5..8 singles, random pairs, fresh seed strings), the reserved T4 task and gemma-2-2b-it, all drawn on fresh sample seeds with a triplicated placebo noise floor. Predictors and thresholds are frozen before any confirmation sample exists.

Unified the label space: one audited classifier and the execution oracle over all three arms. Novelty is reframed as off-menu correct share plus counts of correct A*/bidirectional/IDDFS/Bellman-Ford/counting programs. Judge-confirmed invention is stated as near-floor by construction on textbook tasks.

Added the user's manifold as a deliverable: centroids sized by implemented count, before/after-ban arrows, coordinates dumped to results/, and PC1 non-idea variance reported. SAE naming (Gemma Scope on gemma-2-2b-it) is demoted to last priority, per the reviewer's ordering.

Instructions to the writer: cite steering neighbours for the selector and random-parity claims (Tan et al. 2024 arXiv 2407.12404; Turner et al. 2023; arXiv 2412.06060; STARS arXiv 2601.22010; arXiv 2511.08305) and state the candidate reasons for disagreement (two-idea menu, 3B, late layers 29-31). Recompute the random-control claim against draw-averaged entropy. Report the A4 Spearman with an exact permutation p. Correct the gens/scored file counts (T1 111/110, T3 81/80).
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: The one strand is a lead. Retest selection on bare-prompt 4+ idea menus and tie it to the same geometry that must predict ban substitution, with a held-out confirmation and powered random controls.
hypothesis_update.title: Temperature Flattens Ideas, Context Reorders Them

plans.title: Does temperature change ideas or just wording?
Where do banned ideas go? (ban arm)
Can internal knobs beat temperature for novel code?

critiques.description: Completeness: the ban arm (gen_art_experiment_2) is reported as having 'failed ... before producing results', but it produced 4,360 generations and labelled 4,210 of them (all but the co-mention lists). data/gen/{T1,T2,T3} contains baseline n=300, ban_r1..r4, ban_top3, ban_top5, ban_rare, placebo, para1_r1 and para2_r1 at n=100 each, forced_<idea> cells at n=10 and co-mention lists at n=50. data/labels/{T1,T2,T3} and logs/label.log carry the labels. Only the oracle (labels carry pass=0.00 because the no-oracle path was used), activation capture (ValueError: accelerate missing) and the analysis stage did not run. Recomputed from the label files: T1 ban_r1 (BFS) gives DFS 66, Other 15, A* 11, Dijkstra 7, BFS 1. T1 ban_top3 gives IDDFS 42, DFS 18, Dijkstra 16, A* 8, with 29/100 still banned. T1 ban_top5 gives IDDFS 42, A* 16, with 38/100 still banned. T2 ban_top3 gives Selection 55, Insertion 42, 0 still banned. T2 ban_top5 gives Counting 45, Heap 26. T3 ban_r1 (Dijkstra) gives Bellman-Ford 55, BFS 19, Dijkstra 12. T3 ban_top3 has 46/100 still banned and ban_top5 61/100. This is the run's only evidence on where banned probability goes, which is the user's 'move to the edge or the opposite side' question, and none of it is in the record.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a ban-arm section with the full per-condition count tables for all three tasks, entropy and still-banned counts, and the forced-idea and co-mention tables, each traced to data/labels/<T>/<cond>.jsonl and logs/label.log. Mark explicitly what did not run (oracle, activations, nested-logit and geometry fit) and why. In the next iteration, run the influence arm's audited AST classifier and oracle over these generations so the two arms share one label space.

critiques.description: Contradiction with the run's own evidence. Conclusion 5 ('Bans are mostly ignored by this 3B model (87% to 95%)'), the open item ('a 3B model may be the wrong place to test substitution structure, since there is little banned mass to redistribute') and the answer to question 7 ('the 3B model mostly ignored the ban') all generalise from one prompt protocol to the model. The ban arm, with the same model, T=0.7 and the same task sentence but no output contract and the wording 'Do not use X, Y or Z.', shows large compliance and structured near-neighbour substitution: BFS/DFS/A* banned leads to IDDFS; Dijkstra banned leads to Bellman-Ford; sorting top-3 banned leads to Selection/Insertion. Compliance also falls with list length on T3 (ban_r1 12% still banned, top-3 46%, top-5 61%), a pattern consistent with the 'naming primes' account [5] and worth recording.
critiques.suggested_action: Withdraw 'bans are mostly ignored by this model'. Replace it with: non-compliance is 87-95% under the contract prompt with list-style wording, and 0-46% under the bare prompt with short-list wording (61% for the T3 top-5 list). The difference is unexplained, and the contract and the ban wording are confounded. Reopen question 7 as 'partially answered: substitution goes to near neighbours (IDDFS for DFS/BFS, Bellman-Ford for Dijkstra) at the behavioural level; geometry not yet run'.

critiques.description: The temperature arm is described only as 'not delivered ... raw generations were not analysed'. data/raw_grid.jsonl holds 3,623 completed generations: the full 3 tasks x T{0.3,0.5,0.7,1.0,1.3,1.6} x top-k{10, none} x n=100 grid, plus greedy and repeat rows. data/raw_seeds.jsonl holds 360 seed-string generations (greedy and T=0.7, 60 per task). logs/chain.log shows GRID EXIT 0 and SEEDS EXIT 0, and only labelling was killed (EXIT 130). The report gives none of these paths or counts. It lists seeds as 'untested' rather than 'generated, unlabelled', and it omits two facts that matter for the user's 'always same seed' protocol: 51% of grid rows hit finish=length at 768 tokens (grid_stdout.log), and vLLM grid bit-reproducibility was 2/20 (data/repro_grid.json).
critiques.suggested_action: Record the arm's actual state, with paths, row counts, the 51% truncation rate and the 2/20 reproducibility. In the next iteration, label raw_grid.jsonl and raw_seeds.jsonl with an existing classifier (the influence arm's protocol/classifier.py, or the arm's own ideaclf with its 41/41 fixtures). Report idea share and Hill-number within/between-idea partitions per (task, T, top-k). This directly answers the user's questions a/b/c and the seeding question at essentially no GPU cost. Also check whether truncation biases labels at high T.

critiques.description: Unrecorded confound: the output contract defines the menu. The influence arm appends a function-signature contract (find_path on an unweighted adjacency dict; shortest_path returning (distance, path)). The user's prompt and the ban arm's prompt are the bare sentence. Bare-prompt T1 (ban arm) gives BFS 60%, DFS 15%, A* 13%, Dijkstra 7%, H = 1.764 bits. Contract T1 gives BFS 68%, DFS 27%, H = 1.145. Bare-prompt T3 gives heapq-Dijkstra 300/300, while contract T3 gives BFS-style relaxation 71/300 and heapq in only 219/300. The report's answer to question 2, the 'narrow-menu fallback', the rank-1 erasure, and the explanation of why flattening 'overshoots the uniform point and selects the minority idea' all rest on a two-idea menu that the contract appears to create. (The two arms' classifiers also differ, so part of the T3 gap could be labelling, which is itself unresolved.)
critiques.suggested_action: Add both baselines side by side in Section 1.4 and state that every influence-arm conclusion is conditional on the contract prompt. In iteration 2, rerun the baseline and the H-dim/A4 settings on the bare prompt, with code-only extraction for the oracle, so the selector finding is tested on a menu of four or more ideas, where 'flatten' and 'select' make different predictions.

critiques.description: The positive mechanistic claims have no nearest-neighbour comparison. Claim 1 says steering directions are selectors, not diversifiers, and claim 3 says matched-norm random directions raise idea entropy about as much as targeted ones. Close published neighbours: Tan et al. 2024 (arXiv 2407.12404, NeurIPS) on steering-vector unreliability and anti-steerability; Turner et al. 2023 [7], whose matched-norm random-vector control barely changed outputs; 'Steering LLMs to Evaluate and Amplify Creativity' (arXiv 2412.06060), which reports a creativity direction that increases diversity; and STARS / Stiefel activation steering (arXiv 2601.22010, ICLR 2026) plus Riemannian activation steering for diverse reasoning (arXiv 2511.08305), which report diversity gains over sampling. The run's random-control parity result conflicts with some of these and would be a contribution only once that comparison is written down.
critiques.suggested_action: For claims 1 and 3, name these neighbours. State what this iteration adds: execution-verified correctness, algorithm-level idea labels rather than lexical diversity, a matched random control and a held-out draw. State where the result disagrees with them (random-direction parity) and give candidate reasons (two-idea menu, 3B model, late layers 29-31).

critiques.description: Claim 3 and Table 19 ('five of the ten highest-entropy eligible settings are random controls') rest on an asymmetric comparison. There are 3 random draws per strength at n=75 per task, against single targeted settings at n=150, and the table ranks individual draws. The best of 27 random cells against 10 targeted cells has a selection advantage, and n=75 entropy estimates are noisier, which favours extremes. The noise floor (11-17% label flips) and the anticonservative bootstrap (0.10/0.15 placebo rejection) mean differences of 0.1-0.3 bits are not resolvable here. The iteration answered this with many extra readouts (Table 16 has 14 columns per setting) over the same small panel, not with more samples.
critiques.suggested_action: Recompute claim 3 against draw-averaged random entropy per strength, with a CI across draws and samples. Report how many targeted settings beat the draw mean. If the claim is retained, spend the next budget on more samples per random draw (n=150) and more draws (at least 5), not on more metrics.

critiques.description: Coverage against the user's request is partial. The user asked for: behavioural analysis first, in the spirit of the repo; temperature questions a/b/c with top-k=10 and a fixed seed; context seeding ('seed=d32qxk4nt43', 'seed=(horse chair roof love)'); whether the model gives the 'average answer'; internal comparison of BFS/DFS/Dijkstra runs with SAE/thought-anchor/NLA-style tools; a path-search manifold coloured by count; and a top-5 ban test of 'edge versus opposite side'. Executed data exist on disk for a/b/c, seeding and the top-5 ban, but are unreported. The manifold exists only as figs/fig_pca_manifold.png without coordinates. No SAE or attribution analysis was attempted, although the plan reserved gemma-2-2b-it for that purpose.
critiques.suggested_action: Name these gaps under 'Open after iteration 1'. Prioritise for iteration 2, in this order: (1) label the temperature and seed generations; (2) write up the ban arm and run the oracle on it; (3) compute the manifold on the ban arm's bare-prompt generations (ban_top5 against baseline centroids at layer 30) using the influence arm's activation code; (4) only then add SAE features, on gemma-2-2b-it with Gemma Scope.

critiques.description: The PCA view (figs/fig_pca_manifold.png) is the run's only partial answer to the user's manifold request, and the report drops it because 'coordinates were not written'. The residuals it was computed from are kept on the run volume (acts/ about 870 MB, caps/ about 926 MB), so the coordinates are recomputable. The figure also shows large non-idea structure: T1 has a spread of about 70 units along PC1 that is not aligned with idea labels, which deserves a note.
critiques.suggested_action: Dump per-condition, per-idea centroid coordinates (PC1, PC2, explained variance) to results/ and add them as a table. Record that PC1 is dominated by non-idea variation.

critiques.description: Claim 6 and the answer to question 8 ('Answered negatively ... zero judge-confirmed novel and correct programs') overreach. The judge only saw passing programs in the catch-all class (70 programs), so passing programs that the AST classifier mapped to a known class were never checked for novelty. And for unweighted and weighted path search, a genuinely new correct algorithm is implausible a priori. A zero on a metric with a floor this hard is weak evidence about the model. The informative observable, off-menu correct share (up to 0.113 for generate-then-select on T1), is barely discussed.
critiques.suggested_action: Rephrase as 'no condition produced a correct program the judge did not recognise; the metric is near-floor by construction on these tasks'. Lead the novelty discussion with off-menu correct share and the A* / bidirectional / IDDFS correct counts per condition.

critiques.description: The A4 Spearman CI looks inconsistent: point estimate 0.486 with 95% CI [-0.029, 0.543] (results.json survival.A4), with the point almost at the upper bound, computed over only 6 strength points. The verdict does not depend on it, but a reader cannot tell how the CI was formed.
critiques.suggested_action: State the bootstrap unit (samples within strength, or strengths) and check the CI. A 6-point Spearman has only a few attainable values, so report the exact permutation p-value instead.

critiques.description: Bookkeeping: Section 1.16 says '111 setting files per task'. gens/ has 111 files on T1 and 81 on T3 (calibration ran on T1 only), and scored/ has 110 and 80 (gts_list.jsonl is stage-1 lists, not scored). The 19,250 total is correct.
critiques.suggested_action: Correct the counts and list the calibration-only files.

dimension_scores.justification: The influence-arm methodology is sound and its numbers reproduce. But conclusion 5 ('Bans are mostly ignored by this 3B model (87% to 95%)') and the answer to user question 7 ('not answerable... 3B model mostly ignored the ban... little banned mass to redistribute') contradict the run's own executed ban-arm data on the same model at the same T=0.7. With the bare prompt, T1 ban_top3 leaves only 29/100 programs on a banned idea, T2 bans are fully obeyed, and T3 ban-Dijkstra sends 55/100 to Bellman-Ford. The answer to question 2 (BFS 68%) and the two-idea menu that drives the 'selector' interpretation hold only under the influence arm's output contract, which the report never names as a confound. By this review's rule, a conclusion that contradicts the run's own evidence scores 1.

Within the influence arm a reader can follow what was done, why, and what came out, and every table is introduced by what it settles. The record misleads about the other two arms, though, and omits paths and counts for their outputs, so a reader cannot see that the data exist.

The influence arm is preserved almost completely. But two of the three executed arms are written up as having no data. The ban arm's full condition grid (bans r1-r4, top-3, top-5, rare, placebo, two paraphrases, forced-idea cells, co-mention lists, across three tasks) and the temperature arm's 3,623-row grid plus 360 seed generations are absent. Those are the parts of the run that bear most directly on the user's questions.

review.overall_assessment:
The influence arm (art_aSN7z8WuA7Ir) is recorded thoroughly and its numbers hold. I recomputed the main ones from scored/{T1,T3}/*.jsonl (recompute.py -> recompute_out.json) and every one matched: baseline T1 BFS 205/DFS 80, pass 0.700; T3 Dijkstra 225/BFS 71, pass 0.373; sweep baseline H = 1.175/0.916 bits; top-3 ban H = 1.404/1.779 with 142/150 and 131/150 programs still using a banned idea; generate-then-select H = 2.549/2.574; H-dim a=0.224 gives DFS 145/150 at pass 0.680; held-out entropy ratios 0.932/1.202; 19,250 generations. Survival verdicts, the classifier audit and judge cost match results/results.json. results_reported is therefore true.

The record is still badly incomplete, and that omission changes conclusions. Section 1.2 says the ban arm 'failed with a model-API streaming error before producing results'. On disk, gen_art_experiment_2 holds 4,360 completed generations, 4,210 of them labelled: 3 tasks x {baseline n=300, ban_r1..r4, ban_top3, ban_top5, ban_rare, placebo, two paraphrased bans, n=100 each}, forced-idea cells (n=10) and co-mention lists (data/gen, data/labels, logs/label.log). That arm used the user's bare prompt with no output contract. Its data contradict the report's claim that 'bans are mostly ignored by this 3B model (87% to 95%)' and its answer to user question 7 ('not answerable'). On T1, ban_top3 leaves only 29/100 programs on a banned idea and moves mass to IDDFS (42/100), the nearest neighbour of DFS. On T3, banning Dijkstra sends 55/100 to Bellman-Ford. Sorting bans are obeyed 100%. Banned mass is redistributed toward near neighbours, which is exactly the substitution question the report says it cannot address. The same data show that the bare-prompt T1 menu has four classes above 3% (BFS 179, DFS 44, A* 39, Dijkstra 22), not two. The report's 'BFS 68%' answer to question 2 and its two-idea menus, which made erasure rank-1 and make the flattening direction 'overshoot' into a selector, are therefore products of the output contract the influence arm imposed. The temperature arm is also not empty. data/raw_grid.jsonl has 3,623 generations covering the full 3 tasks x 6 temperatures x top-k {10, none} x 100 grid, and data/raw_seeds.jsonl has 360 seed-string generations. Only labelling was interrupted (chain.log: LG/LS EXIT 130). Yet the report lists seeds as 'untested' and gives no paths, counts, truncation rate (51% hit the 768-token limit) or vLLM bit-reproducibility (2/20). Because a stated conclusion contradicts the run's own executed evidence, soundness is 1 and the record is blocking until the ban arm is written up and claim 5 and question 7 are corrected.

Separately, the positive mechanistic finding (steering selects among known ideas and does not diversify; matched-norm random directions do about as well) is not compared with its nearest published neighbours. Those are Tan et al. 2024 on steering-vector unreliability, steering for creativity (arXiv 2412.06060), and the STARS / Riemannian diversity-steering line (2601.22010, 2511.08305), which report diversity gains from steering. Coverage of the user's request is partial: questions a/b/c, seeding, the manifold, and 'move to the edge or the opposite side' all have executed data on disk that the record does not use.
strengths: The influence arm is fully traceable and reproducible. Every table in Sections 1.4-1.15 matches results/results.json and the scored files, and I recomputed the headline numbers exactly (baseline, ban, generate-then-select, H-dim takeover, held-out ratios 0.932/1.202, ban non-compliance 142/150 and 131/150).

Pre-registered survival rules were frozen (results/rules.json, 15:39:37). Selection on indices 0..99 was followed by a fresh-seed held-out draw, a protocol that removes winner's-curse bias, and the negative outcome is reported as the prescribed 'prompting ceiling' without spin.

Strong controls and honesty about noise: matched-norm random directions and projections, a batch-composition noise-floor rerun (11-17% label flips), a placebo test showing the bootstrap CIs are anticonservative (0.10/0.15 against a nominal 0.05), and an independent re-derivation (verify_headline.py, 147/147 oracle agreement).

Dead ends inside the influence arm are kept and labelled with the tables that killed them: flattening, menu erasure, the unusualness dial, and early-token probes. Section 1.6 explains clearly why the gen1..8 probe sits at the majority baseline (0.433 = mean of per-task majority recalls) and why the late-window fallback was used.

The manipulation checks (Table 24) separate 'the internal readout changed' from 'the behaviour changed'. LEACE removes decodability while the outputs stay BFS/DFS/Dijkstra, a useful dissociation that is properly recorded.
The classifier audit gives the full confusion matrix (kappa 0.684) and names the main confusions (rule SPFA against judge BFS), so readers can judge label validity.

strategies.expected_outcome: After this iteration: (1) a ranked, pre-registered comparison of five candidate mechanisms across three knob families on identical evidence (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, three tasks, fixed seeds, one validated classifier), with one survivor or an explicit 'ambiguous' verdict per family and the margins on which each decision rests; (2) direct, quantified answers to the user's questions: (a)/(b)/(c) via the alpha/beta Hill partition under temperature and top-k=10, whether seeding helps via sigma_seed vs utility gap, 'mean vs mode', and 'ban the top 5: edge or opposite side' with the manifold figure; (3) reusable building blocks for iteration 2, namely labelled generation corpora, the classifier, oracle and judge-audit code with kappa, cached activations, probe weights, steering, erasure and typicality vectors, and the commitment positions. NOTHING IS CLAIMED FROM THE SCREEN ALONE. The survivors are confirmed in iteration 2 on evidence that this iteration never touches: a second model family, gemma-2-2b-it (which also brings Gemma Scope SAEs for naming the features the survivor moves), and a held-out fourth task (k-th smallest element / selection, whose menu is quickselect, heapq, sort-then-index and median-of-medians). Confirmation means re-running only the surviving arm's pre-registered rule with the same margins. The reserved task's labels come from the same deterministic classifier extended with selection classes plus the execution oracle, both written and judge-audited this iteration, so the iteration-2 confirmation has its labelling pipeline ready and only needs to generate.
strategies.objective: Run a pre-registered three-arm screen on one open-weight instruction model (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) and identical tasks, prompts and idea classifier. It decides which mechanistic account of 'LLM creativity' survives on each of the three knob families the user asked about. TEMPERATURE: a single early commitment fork with a readable utility vector, where heat flattens but never reorders (H), vs gradual multi-path commitment, where heat reorders toward 'entropic' ideas (A1). BANS: nested-logit substitution to the banned idea's nearest internal neighbour (H) vs repulsion to the far side of the idea manifold (A2) vs plain IIA renormalisation (null). INTERNAL INFLUENCE: flattening the utility vector at the commitment layer (H) vs erasing the menu subspace (A3) vs a task-general 'unusualness' direction (A4), all against tuned temperature, novelty prompts, bans and random-direction controls at matched correctness. The output is a ranked comparison with effect sizes, one survivor per knob family, and reusable building blocks (classified generations, activations, classifier and oracle code). Iteration 2 then confirms the survivors on the reserved model and task.
strategies.rationale: The hypothesis bundles three separable claims, and each has a rival alternate that predicts the OPPOSITE observable on the same data. That makes a cheap wide screen decisive in a way a deep test of H alone could not be. (1) H predicts straight Arrhenius lines, no top-3 reversals for T<=1.3, and a sharp single fork; A1 predicts curvature, reversals at high T, and many partial forks whose count predicts which ideas gain with heat. One temperature grid plus forking-path resampling settles it. (2) H predicts that post-ban mass lands closer in activation space to the banned centroids than the baseline average; A2 predicts it lands farther; IIA predicts no geometric structure. One ban set with geometry from unbanned runs settles it. (3) H, A3 and A4 are three different internal edits that can be put on one Pareto plot of idea entropy and outside-menu correct share vs pass rate, against the knobs practitioners actually use. Each arm answers a concrete question from the user's request. Arm 1 covers the a/b/c questions (ideas vs phrasings under temperature and top-k=10), via an alpha/beta Hill-number partition, and the 'mean vs mode' question, via a utility-vector readout. Arm 2 covers the 'ban the top 5: edge or opposite side of the manifold?' question, with the manifold plot. Arm 3 covers 'can we make LLMs give truly novel solutions?', with the seed-shock comparison as a cheap add-on. All arms aim at positive, lead-able results. Arm 1 targets a quantitative temperature law, Arm 2 a measured IIA violation with a geometric predictor (no prior work studies substitution structure among ideas), and Arm 3 an internal knob that dominates temperature at matched correctness. A null in any arm is still a clean mechanistic finding, because the rival in that arm wins. This is the first iteration and no dataset exists, so each experiment generates its own data under the shared protocol and saves it for iteration 2.
strategies.title: Screening rival theories of LLM idea choice

artifacts.layman_summary: We relabel about 14,000 programs written by a small open model and test, with predictions frozen in advance, whether more randomness or a random 'seed' phrase makes it choose different algorithms. Mostly it does not.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_4
artifacts.summary: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, bare prompts (T1 path search, T2 sorting, T3 weighted shortest path). PROVIDES: (1) a unified label ledger results/labels_unified.jsonl of 13,968 programs: iteration-1 grid 3,623, seed rows 360, ban arm 4,210 (the planned __topup files do not exist), new P1 re-draw 3,615 and fresh seeds 2,160. It uses the canonical v1 classifier (hash d0d321215bc2; 4,210/4,210 stored labels reproduce), sandboxed oracle pass/status for every program (results/oracle_results.jsonl), and a classifier audit: v1 vs blind gpt-4.1-mini kappa 0.84 [0.78,0.89], judge-judge 0.92, AST classifier 0.44-0.76; spend $0.042. (2) Ban-arm screen tables (results/screen_tables.json): compliance, pass, off-menu correct share, Fisher/Holm regularity candidates (T1 ban SPFA->DFS 17->1; T2 ban Quick->Bubble 43->15; T2 ban Insertion->Bubble 43->1), grid-vs-P1 wording check (T2 JSD 0.107, p<1e-4). (3) Claim C1, temperature law: FAILS on screen and re-draw. R^2>=0.85 is not met by all lines, though a simulation shows R^2<0.85 in 25-87% of draws under a TRUE linear law. There are top-3 reversals at T<=1.3, and the alpha/beta slope ratio is 0.6-2.6 (<3). T1 intercepts are significantly <0, so it is not a pure fixed-utility scale model. Frozen out of sample (sha d1dabe95), the law beats the fixed-utility baseline on T1 (MAE 0.040 vs 0.073) but not on T2 (0.100 vs 0.028). The user's (a)/(b)/(c) table: few ideas (E[ideas among 10] 2-4) with near-max distinct phrasings already at T=0.3 on T1; T rises ideas slowly; T=1.6 without top-k degenerates (93-95% truncated, Unparseable/Other). (4) Truncation audit: continuing 150 truncated rows flips 10.7% of labels; 0/20 prefixes reproduce on regeneration. (5) Claim C3, seed shocks: FAILS. Frozen behavioural predictor (sha 1cffcec3; the readout failed its coverage gate) vs observed greedy flip: T1 0.28 vs 0.25 ok, T2 0.39 vs 0.017 fail, T3 0.00 ok. Seed strings NARROW rather than diversify ideas (T=0.7 entropy T1 -0.34 bits, T2 -0.68 bits, CIs exclude 0), although they displace the residual stream 1.5-3x more than a ban sentence. (6) Frozen C4 reference (results/frozen_c4_reference.json, sha 783778b0): correct off-menu share stays <=0.08 at any T (T2 best T=1.3). All headline numbers are re-derived independently with placebo controls in results/verify_headline.json. method_out.json holds 4 datasets (C1 re-draw cells with frozen-law vs fixed-utility vs no-temperature predictions; C3 seed strings; ban conditions; program ledger) plus all verdicts in metadata.
artifacts.title: Does temperature or a seed phrase change the algorithm an LLM picks?

artifacts.layman_summary: Tests whether telling a code-writing AI 'do not use method X' works by nudging its internal state toward specific alternatives, and finds the ban is instead re-read from the prompt while writing.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_5
artifacts.summary: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, bare coding prompts (T1 path search, T2 sorting, T3 weighted shortest path, new T4 k-th smallest). Tests whether a ban's prompt-suffix displacement Delta_h = h(ban)-h(placebo) (5 chat-template suffix tokens, layers 32-34 chosen by probe) predicts which ideas gain share. Seven one-scalar predictors (A IIA, B Delta_h displacement, C nested geometry, D/D2 bge embeddings, D3 Qwen name lexical, E co-mention) share one floor+compliance model, are fit by LOBO on 27 screen bans, FROZEN by sha256+git commit, then scored on 5,930 never-generated vLLM confirmation generations (n=100/cell). RESULTS (re-derived independently in verify_headline.py): C2a PASS - regularity violations in 6 bans (T1 Bellman-Ford, Greedy best-first, IDDFS; T2 Counting, Radix, Shell; 8/46 Holm cells), 0/45 on placebo-vs-placebo and 0 in 20 shuffled reps; e.g. banning near-zero-rate greedy best-first moves A* 3%->58%, BFS 63%->23%. Sign accuracy B 0.83 (balanced 0.79) vs IIA 0.65 (0.50). C2b FAIL - B vs IIA mean JSD on T1-T3 bans 0.188 vs 0.207 (9.2% reduction, CI [-0.6%,19.6%], target 20%), top-hit 0.20; B beats external bge embeddings D/D2 (CIs exclude 0); T4 pure transfer B worse than IIA (-25%). C2c FAIL - adding Delta_h at the suffix (prefill, layer 32), restore, 35-layer suffix ceiling and Stolfo all-position add all give recovery ~0 (mean R -0.001; random 5-draw -0.006). Exploratory decode-time attention knockout of the ban sentence restores placebo behaviour (mean restoration 0.72): the ban is read from the sentence tokens during generation, not from the prompt-final state. Logit lens of Delta_h: top tokens 'while/although/another/new', banned name median rank ~17.6k (no priming). Mention 'You may use X' drives X strongly (A* 3%->95%); ban vs mention Delta_h cos 0.70-0.85 on user tokens, 0.06-0.38 at suffix. Edge-vs-far-side statistic: no consistent direction (33/56 positive). T4 classifier v1+T4 audited by gpt-4.1-mini (kappa 0.79, $0.015). Outputs: method_out.json (6,740 examples, predict_iia/disp/embed/... = frozen P of observed label), results/*.json (frozen predictors/predictions, scores, regularity, transplant, edge, lens, manifold_coords), figures/, data/conf (all generations+labels), data/transplant. Caveats: single model family, one wording per ban, beta near grid edge.
artifacts.title: Do idea bans steer an LLM's internal state?

artifacts.layman_summary: Pushing a model's internals away from its default algorithm makes it pick one specific neighbouring algorithm rather than more varied ones, and simply asking works better.
artifacts.name: gen_art_experiment_6
artifacts.summary: Pre-registered test of whether activation steering SELECTS or FLATTENS the algorithm an LLM writes, plus a ban-displacement test on a second model family. A (re-analysis of iteration-1 influence arm, results/reanalysis_contract.json): vs the DRAW-AVERAGED random entropy (Miller-Madow, n-matched, hierarchical bootstrap) 3/18 targeted settings beat it, 5/18 are below (selection), 10/18 undetermined -> claim 3 'random = targeted' does not hold as stated; A4 Spearman exact permutation p=0.36 (T1), 0.66 (T3). B (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, HF engine, bare prompts T1 path search / T2 sorting; frozen rules with SHA256): difference-in-means d_away is a SELECTOR on both tasks, replicated on a fresh-seed re-draw: T1 BFS 61%->13% and A* (frozen predicted gainer) 57%/63% but pass 0.31->0.17; T2 Bubble 62%->0-1%, Quick 65%/68% (predicted), pass 0.92; vs 5 matched-norm random draws: non-mode share +0.54 (T1) / +0.41 (T2) above draw mean, T2 entropy -0.71 bits below draw mean. Prompting beats steering for off-menu ideas (d_j: 0-1% IDDFS/Bellman-Ford/Counting vs 92-100% when asked; exception d_Heap 91%). C4 (off-menu correct >=3x best temperature) passes only on T2. HF vs vLLM baseline JSD 0.009/0.001 (consistent). Probe band layers 32-34; decodability flat across layers (name-token readout). C (gemma-2-2b-it, HF eager, reduced n): frozen displacement logit GEOM loses to IIA on 14 held-out bans (mean JSD 0.121 vs 0.088, EXT 0.093; gain -0.71, CI [-1.29,-0.23]); top-substitute hit 7%; regularity violated in 1/72 cells; placebo sentence alone shifts T2 Bubble 81%->Merge ~55%; temperature law near-linear in 1/T on T2 (R2 0.93-0.96), T=0.3 gives 1 idea with 19 phrasings; Delta_h transplant at L*=13 recovers 0.06 (T2), C2c fails; SAE FVU 0.61 (unreliable, descriptive). Audit kappa 0.94 T2, 0.39 T1 (label-limited). Files: results/verdicts.json (all verdicts), selector_tables.json, gemma_bans.json, gemma_temperature.json, transplant.json, audit.json, sae_latents.json, verify.json (independent re-derivation + placebo checks), deviations.json; method_out.json has 9,720 generations (Qwen+gemma, T1/T2) with v1 label, oracle status and off-menu-correct flags. Kept on the run volume only: data/acts/ (window activations) and results/*.pt (frozen vectors/centroids/Delta_h).
artifacts.title: Does steering pick ideas or spread them?

hypothesis_update.coverage_statement: The next round answers how much prompt instructions matter and where mass goes when top ideas are banned (edge vs far side), how creativity manifests inside (commitment token, attention heads), the seeding question with the user's literal strings, and whether any knob reaches unusual ideas; the temperature (a)/(b)/(c) answers are already in hand.
key_changes: Recorded as DEAD, one sentence each: the temperature law (C1), the seed-shock predictor (C3), the 20% geometry-over-IIA claim (C2b), the Delta_h transplant (C2c), nearest-neighbour steering prediction and centroid steering to off-menu ideas.

Kept the two leads and made them the object of the round. (1) Bans move mass to specific unbanned ideas and violate regularity: 8/46 confirmation cells vs 0/45 placebo. (2) Away-from-mode directions select one idea (A* 57/63%, quicksort 65/68%) rather than flatten.

Answered the reviewer's priming confound head-on with a pre-registered MENTION DECOMPOSITION. Neutral mention 'X is one known algorithm.', 'You may use X.' and an out-of-domain mention are run against each violating ban, with a frozen rule separating name priming (R1) from prohibition-specific displacement (R2). Both outcomes are positive answers.

Added a parameter-free behavioural predictor, 'ban = neutral-mention distribution minus X', scored on held-out never-generated bans against IIA on the concurrent placebo. It gives the user's edge-vs-far-side question a quantitative answer: mass goes where the names send it.

Turned the exploratory knockout into a controlled mechanism test: random equal-length span knockout, the placebo-sentence-knockout target, K/V patching of the ban sentence's states into an equal-length placebo, knockout on top-3 and T3 Dijkstra, and head-group localisation with an OV logit lens of neighbour names. This answers PASTA-style neighbours by localising the heads.

Added a SINK TEST for the selector: 20 random directions plus the off-target direction and rare-idea bans, to check whether A* is the task's runner-up attractor and not a geometric prediction. Also added a logit lens of d_away for the 'A*' and 'quick' tokens and non-truncated label restriction.
Added forking-path commitment localisation (the user's thought-anchor question), predicting commitment at the first algorithm-name or data-structure token.
Seeds: run the user's two literal strings, plus an SSoT-style instructed seed, as a discriminating test of why prepended seeds narrow while model-used seeds diversify in String Seed of Thought.

Restricted gemma ban verdicts to T2. Listed every reviewer write-up correction: question 7 status, sign-accuracy figure, B_screenP0 asymmetry, code-stop label sensitivity, KNOCKOUT_PLACEBO_SENT cells, probe-band tables, T4 mean points, massive-dimension zeroing, extra07 rows, callable-pass rates, and the question 6/8 wording.
Title changed from 'Temperature Flattens Ideas, Context Reorders Them'. Temperature was shown NOT to flatten by a law. The surviving content is that context names reorder and heat does not.
hypothesis_update.move_rationale: All three strands are leads. Deepen the ban/selector leads by attacking their shared confound (name priming) with mention controls, K/V patching and sink tests; both outcomes are informative.
hypothesis_update.title: Naming an Algorithm Moves Ideas; Heat Does Not

plans.title: Labelling every run, then testing temperature and seeds
Bans as nudges to the idea state

critiques.suggested_action: Run 'You may use X.' and neutral-mention controls (for example 'X is one known algorithm.') at n = 100 for the six violating bans (T1 Bellman-Ford, greedy best-first, IDDFS; T2 counting, radix, shell). If the neutral mention reproduces the A*/Dijkstra/merge-sort gains, record regularity violations as mention-priming of neighbours and rewrite conclusion 4. Also logit-lens the ban displacement for the neighbour names (A*, Dijkstra), not only the banned name. Until then, state both readings in Section 2.8.

critiques.description:
The answer to the user's question 7 ('mass goes to the banned ideas' internal neighbours on path search, IDDFS sits next to BFS and DFS') is not supported by Table 63's own tests:
- Of the 9 T1 screen statistics, only paraphrase 1 reaches permutation p < 0.05 (p = 0.029); the rest are p = 0.065 to 0.67.
- The bootstrap CIs that exclude 0 resample samples with the centroids fixed, the same kind of interval that gave the misleading Spearman CI in iteration 1.
- For the user's literal case, the top-5 ban, the T1 statistic is -0.035 (p = 0.67).
- Across all 56 bans, 33 are positive, which is roughly a coin flip.
- The supporting manifold remark (top-5 mean point moves 'toward the upper middle; it does not cross to the far side') compares condition mean points that include the prompt's own shift. The placebo alone moves the T1 mean point by 8 PC1 units (Table 66: baseline -26.2 vs placebo -18.2), so mean-point movement conflates prompt displacement with idea composition.
- Centroids for the unwritten ideas (Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, IDDFS, bidirectional, greedy) come only from forced 'using X.' prompts, whose agreement with natural centroids is weak (Spearman 0.36 on T1).
critiques.suggested_action: Change the status of question 7 to: 'no direction is detectable by the pre-specified permutation test on any task; top-5 statistic near zero on all three tasks'. Drop 'internal neighbours on path search' from Sections 2.10 and the closing. If a direction claim is wanted, pre-register a pooled sign or permutation test across all 56 bans, and compute the manifold mean point from the idea-composition-weighted baseline centroids rather than from ban-run activations, so prompt shift is removed.

critiques.description:
Completeness and rigor of the knockout result. 'The ban is applied while the program is being written' is promoted to established conclusion 2.10.5 and to the closing section, but it rests on one exploratory manipulation: n = 60, four bans, no pre-registration. transplant.json contains a control cell the report omits, KNOCKOUT_PLACEBO_SENT (knocking out attention to the placebo sentence in the placebo run):
- T1: BFS 42, A* 3, DFS 11, restoration 0.89 and 0.62.
- T2: Bubble 52, Quick 6, Selection 2, restoration 0.78 and 0.86.
The knocked-out ban runs restore toward the no-sentence distribution rather than the placebo. T2 ban_rare knockout gives Bubble 24/Quick 23 against placebo-knockout Bubble 52, so restoration on that ban is partial despite the 0.80 score. There is no random-span knockout control, so 'removing attention to any 6-10 prompt tokens shifts the output' is not ruled out. The transplants patched only the 5 suffix positions, or added the suffix Δh at all positions, never the sentence tokens' own key/value states, so 'not the prompt-final state' is tested but 'not the sentence-token states' is not.
critiques.suggested_action: Add the KNOCKOUT_PLACEBO_SENT cells to Table 61 and discuss them. Run, at n = 100: (i) a random equal-length span knockout on the ban prompt; (ii) K/V patching of the ban sentence's cached keys and values into a placebo run of equal token length; and (iii) the knockout on the remaining screen bans, including top-3 and T3 Dijkstra, which were 'not run'. Until then, list conclusion 5 under 'supported by one exploratory manipulation', not 'established'.

critiques.description: Code-stop label sensitivity is recorded only as an exp6 deviation and is not propagated to iteration 1. exp6 codestop_check.json shows that stopping generation at the first closing code fence changes the v1 idea label in 13% of T1 programs (agreement 0.87; T2 0.967). Iteration 1's influence arm used exactly this 'code-block early stop for all conditions' (Section 1.3). Every iteration-1 idea count is therefore a label of the first code block, while every iteration-2 count labels the final program. The truncation audit makes the same point from the other side: the model writes a short bubble sort first, then a merge sort. This is a second confound between the contract arm and the bare-prompt arms, on top of the contract and classifier differences, and it bears on the 'two-idea menu' comparison in Table 29.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a marked correction in Section 1.3/1.4 stating that iteration-1 labels classify the first code block and that code-stop changes 13% of T1 labels on the bare prompt. Add the codestop agreement to Table 29's notes. In Section 2.3, state explicitly which program the v1 classifier labels when a response contains several (first, last, or longest), since this decides what counts as 'the idea'.

critiques.description:
Two new positive, non-obvious claims in iteration 2 have no nearest-neighbour comparison.

(1) 'Seed strings narrow ideas' (Section 2.6, conclusion 3). The closest published result predicts the opposite direction: String Seed of Thought (Misaki & Akiba, arXiv 2510.21150, ICLR 2026) has the model generate a random string and manipulate it to choose an answer, and reports better distribution faithfulness and NoveltyBench diversity. The repo that inspired the run reported that random context seeds changed nothing. The report must say why a prepended, user-supplied seed narrows while a model-generated, explicitly used seed diversifies. The candidate difference is that the model is never told to use the seed.

(2) 'The ban is read from the sentence tokens during decoding, not from a prompt-final state' (Section 2.8). The closest neighbours are attention-to-instruction work: PASTA (Zhang et al., ICLR 2024, arXiv 2311.02262), which steers instruction-following by reweighting specific heads' attention to user-marked instruction spans; instruction-drift and attention-decay work on system prompts; and Stolfo et al. [17], which is cited only as a transplant variant. As it stands the knockout result restates what PASTA's premise already implies: instruction adherence runs through decode-time attention to the instruction span.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short neighbour paragraph to Sections 2.6 and 2.8. Name SSoT and the repo's null seed result and state what this run adds: algorithm-level labels with execution, a greedy flip rate, and the finding that prepended seeds displace the residual 1.1-3.2x more than a ban yet change ideas less. Name PASTA and state what the knockout adds: a negative transplant at the prompt-final state on two models. As a cheap discriminating test, run an SSoT-style instruction ('use the seed to choose an approach') at n = 100 per task to see whether instruction to use the seed reverses the narrowing.

critiques.description: Asymmetric post-hoc comparison in Section 2.8. The text says 'anchoring the displacement predictor on the screen placebo instead of the confirmation placebo lowers its JSD to 0.165 ... Part of the error is therefore the placebo itself drifting'. Only predictor B gets the screen-placebo variant (B_screenP0 in predictor_scores_conf.json); there is no A_screenP0. Placebo drift would affect IIA too, so 0.165 is not comparable with IIA's 0.207 and does not show the drift is B's handicap. The same section quotes sign accuracy '83% (balanced 0.79)' for the primary paragraph, but that is the all-33-ban figure; the T1-T3 primary value is 0.795, balanced 0.776.
critiques.suggested_action: Compute IIA and the other predictors anchored on the screen placebo and report them beside B_screenP0, or drop the drift inference. Correct the sign-accuracy figure in the primary paragraph and in conclusion 2.10.4 to the T1-T3 value, or label 0.83 as all-33.

critiques.description:
The specificity of the selector result is overstated.
- A* is the common sink for many structured perturbations on T1: the off-target real direction (sorting's away vector) also makes A* the top non-mode idea (40/150, Table 70; verdicts.json off_s2 A* 0.267); banning Dijkstra raises A* to 34; banning greedy best-first raises it to 58; the iteration-1 novelty direction raised A*.
- 'The projection predicted A*' is therefore weaker evidence of geometric prediction than stated.
- The SELECT rule accepted a gainer from either of two frozen rankings (predicted_gainers = [A*, IDDFS]), which loosens it.
- The T1 s2 operating point fails the frozen pass precondition (0.17 vs 0.25 needed) with 78% truncation, and A* outputs truncate far more often than BFS (odds ratio 182).
- The commitment-window features include name tokens (probe decodability flat from layer 1), so the away direction may be partly a lexical 'A*/quicksort' direction.
critiques.suggested_action: State that the off-target direction also selects A*, and that the SELECT rule accepted either ranking's top gainer. Logit-lens the away-from-mode direction and report the rank of the 'A*' and 'quick' tokens, as was done for the ban displacement. Report the T1 s2 label distribution restricted to non-truncated outputs.

critiques.description:
Coverage of the user's request is still partial on the interpretability half.
- The user asked to 'analyze the internals, all the runs that produced BFS vs DFS vs Dijkstra' with thought anchors, NLA or SAE. Forking-path or thought-anchor analysis has not run in any iteration. The only SAE step (gemma, FVU 0.61) is marked unreliable. No attribution or circuit analysis was attempted.
- The question 'how does creativity manifest inside the model' is answered only negatively: no single prompt-final carrier, and directions select.
- The user's two literal seed strings ('seed=d32qxk4nt43', 'seed=(horse chair roof love)') were never run, though they cost minutes.
- Questions 1-5 and 7 are answered behaviourally.
The closing section's status list marks question 8 'Answered' on a metric the report itself calls near-floor by construction.
critiques.suggested_action: Mark question 6 'not answered at the circuit or feature level'. Run the two literal seed strings at n = 100 per task with greedy decoding (cheap). For the next iteration, run forking-path resampling on BFS/DFS/A* baseline programs to locate per-sample commitment, then attention-head patching on the knockout cells, as Section 2.11 proposes. For SAEs, use transcoders or SAEs trained on the instruct model, or report FVU per layer to find a usable layer. Rephrase question 8 as 'answered for off-menu known ideas; not testable for genuine invention on these tasks'.

critiques.description:
Some result objects and processing steps on disk are not written up:
- Per-layer probe-band curves: exp6 qwen_probe_band.json and gemma_probe_band.json, and exp5 band_selection.json. These are summarised in one sentence although they justify the band choice.
- The T4 manifold coordinates and the UMAP/LDA manifold variants (exp5 manifold_coords.json, figures/manifold_*_umap, manifold_T4_lda). Table 64 covers T4 but Table 65 has no T4 placebo or ban mean points.
- exp6 fig_centroid_map.
- The zeroing of 10 massive-activation dimensions before every centroid and displacement (geometry_checks.json).
- The 200 extra T = 0.7 'extra07' rows per task in the re-draw that form the n = 300 unseeded reference of Table 49, absent from Table 27's description.
critiques.suggested_action: Add a short probe-band table per artifact (layer, balanced accuracy, shuffled). Add T4 mean points to Table 66 or state their exclusion. Note the massive-dimension zeroing in Section 2.8 with the dimension list. Add the extra07 rows to Table 27.

critiques.description:
Pass rates on the bare prompt are low and partly measure the oracle's ability to call a program:
- T1 Qwen baseline pass is 0.27-0.31, with 41 not callable and 38 load errors in 300.
- Gemma T1 pass is 0.13, with 62/150 not callable and 87% truncated at 768 tokens.
The off-menu-correct test, the s2 pass precondition and the 'pass falls with T' statements on T1 therefore mix algorithmic correctness with entry-point discovery and truncation. Gemma's T1 labels are flagged (kappa 0.39), but its T1 ban, transplant and temperature results still enter the conclusions ('on gemma it loses to IIA').
critiques.suggested_action: Report pass rate among callable, non-truncated programs alongside raw pass for each T1 cell used in a verdict. Restrict the gemma ban-prediction verdict to T2, or state that the gemma T1 half is label-limited and underpowered (noise floor 18 pp at n = 50).

dimension_scores.justification: The numbers recompute exactly and the core behavioural findings are well controlled: bans are obeyed on the bare prompt, temperature adds ideas slowly, seeds narrow, and the away-from-mode direction selects against 5 random draws. Several interpretive claims outrun their tests. The regularity result is read as choice-set displacement although an in-domain priming alternative is uncontrolled. The 'internal neighbours on path search' edge answer is not significant by its own permutation tests. The decode-time knockout is exploratory (n = 60, 4 bans) and its placebo-sentence knockout control is unreported. The screen-placebo predictor variant is compared asymmetrically. The code-stop label sensitivity (13% on T1) was never propagated back to iteration 1.

A researcher not on the run can follow why each iteration-2 artifact was run (Section 2.1 ties each one to a review objection and a revised-hypothesis claim), what came out, and which tables settle what. The report is very long, and some summary statements mix subsets. For example, 'sign accuracy 83%' is quoted in the T1-T3 primary paragraph but is the all-33-ban figure; the T1-T3 value is 0.795. Some processing steps that change the numbers are not stated where the numbers appear: 10 massive-activation dimensions were zeroed before the centroids and displacements, and the 200 extra T = 0.7 re-draw rows form the n = 300 unseeded reference.

review.overall_assessment:
Iteration 2 fixes almost every MUST-FIX item from the blocking review, and the record is now largely complete and traceable. The ban arm and the temperature/seed arm are written up in full with their tables (Sections 2.4 to 2.6). The contract-prompt confound is stated and corrections are marked in place throughout Section 1. The random-parity claim is re-analysed against the draw-averaged random entropy, and the ban-compliance conclusion is withdrawn. Steering neighbours are named, the Spearman CI is replaced by an exact permutation p-value, and the file counts are corrected. I recomputed the headline numbers from the artifacts' own files, and they match.

- **Ban arm** (gen_art_experiment_4 labels_unified.jsonl + oracle_results.jsonl). T1 baseline BFS 179/DFS 44/A* 39/Dijkstra 22, H = 1.764 bits, pass 0.27. T1 top-3 ban: IDDFS 42, still banned 29. T3 ban_r1: Bellman-Ford 55. T3 top-5: still banned 61. T2 top-5: Counting 45/Heap 26.
- **Temperature re-draw.** T1 at T = 0.3 to 1.0: H 1.698 to 1.962 bits, pass 0.49 to 0.19.
- **Seed strings.** T1 seeded H 1.283 vs unseeded 1.620; T2 0.857 vs 1.534.
- **Ban predictors** (exp5 predictor_scores_conf.json). Mean JSD on the 22 T1-T3 bans is 0.2069 for IIA vs 0.1878 for the displacement predictor, a 9.2% reduction. T4: 0.096 vs 0.120.
- **Regularity.** 8/46 cells violated; 0/45 on placebo-vs-placebo.
- **Knockout.** Mean restoration 0.719.
- **Gemma** (exp6 gemma_bans.json). IIA 0.0878 vs GEOM 0.1215 vs EXT 0.0931.
- **Verdicts** (exp6 verdicts.json). Counts 3/5/10; selector SELECT on both draws.

The results are real and recomputed, so results_reported is true.

Remaining problems are interpretive overreach and some omissions, not missing experiments:
- **Regularity reading.** The 'regularity violation' result is read as a choice-model violation of the form 'do something other than the obvious'. The ban prompt also names an in-domain algorithm, so a semantic-neighbour priming account explains the same data. No in-domain mention control exists for those bans.
- **Edge statistic.** The 'mass goes to internal neighbours on path search' answer to the user's edge-vs-far-side question is not supported by its own permutation tests: only 1 of 9 T1 statistics has p < 0.05, and the user's literal top-5 case is -0.035.
- **Knockout.** The finding rests on n = 60 and 4 bans, and its one control (KNOCKOUT_PLACEBO_SENT, in transplant.json) is not reported.
- **Code-stop.** Exp6 found that the code-stop rule changes 13% of T1 labels. Iteration 1's influence arm used that rule for every condition, and no correction was propagated into Section 1.
- **Asymmetric comparison.** The screen-placebo anchoring variant is applied only to the displacement predictor, not to IIA.
- **Novelty.** The two new positive claims (seed strings narrow ideas; bans act through decode-time attention to the instruction) are not compared with their nearest neighbours: String Seed of Thought (ICLR 2026) and PASTA/instruction-attention work.

Coverage of the user's request is partial. The behavioural questions (a/b/c, BFS default, seeding, prompt instructions, top-5 ban) are answered. The interpretability half is thin: SAE marked unreliable, no thought anchors or forking paths, no NLA or attribution, and the user's two literal seed strings were not tested.
strengths: Every must-fix from the previous blocking review was acted on. The two 'not delivered' arms are now fully written up with per-condition tables (Tables 27-52). Corrections are marked in place in Sections 1.2, 1.4, 1.9, 1.10, 1.12, 1.16 and 1.17, so the chronology is preserved rather than silently rewritten.

The numbers are traceable and correct. Every headline I recomputed from labels_unified.jsonl, oracle_results.jsonl, predictor_scores_conf.json, regularity.json, transplant.json, gemma_bans.json and verdicts.json matches the report to the reported precision.

Screening discipline is real. Predictors, temperature laws, seed predictors, off-menu references and selector rules were frozen by sha256 or git commit before confirmation data existed. Confirmation used never-generated conditions, a reserved task (k-th smallest) and a second model family.

Dead ends are kept and labelled with the evidence that killed them. The temperature law, seed-shock prediction, the transplant, geometry as a substitution predictor, nearest-neighbour steering prediction and random parity each have a named killing table.

The random-control re-analysis does what was asked: draw-averaged random entropy, Miller-Madow, n-matched seeds, a hierarchical bootstrap, and a specification-sensitivity table (Table 68). The new selector test spends the budget on samples (5 random draws, n = 150, a fresh-seed re-draw), not on more metrics.

The R^2 >= 0.85 criterion is honestly shown to be weak with a simulation under a true linear law (Table 42), and the curvature LR test is reported as the better check. This is a good example of reading a pre-registered criterion for what it can and cannot detect.
The HF vs vLLM engine consistency check (JSD 0.009/0.001) and the truncation-continuation audit (10.7% label flips) put two otherwise silent measurement risks on record.

strategies.expected_outcome: At the end of this final iteration the pool holds three things. (1) One audited label space with execution correctness over about 8.3k existing plus about 20k new bare-prompt programs, including the full ban-arm screen tables the reviewer required. (2) Pre-registered, hash-frozen verdicts on C1 (temperature law: screen grid + truncation-free re-draw + gemma), C2a/b/c (regularity violations, internal vs IIA vs external-embedding prediction on held-out bans and the reserved task T4, and the causal transplant/subtraction against random and off-target displacements on Qwen and gemma), C3 (seed shock prediction on fresh seeds) and C4 (off-menu correct share of steering and transplant vs the frozen best temperature). (3) The user's deliverables: the a/b/c 'ideas x phrasings' table under top-k=10; the seeding answer; the mode-not-mean answer; the idea manifold sized by count with before/after-ban arrows and coordinates; the edge-vs-opposite-side answer per task family; and a descriptive Gemma Scope account of what a ban primes. The verdict rule is the hypothesis's: CONFIRM if C2 and at least two of C1, C3 and C4 hold on confirmation data; otherwise each failed criterion is reported as its named disconfirmer. In every case the paper has a reproducible ledger and the corrected iteration-1 claims (draw-averaged random parity, permutation p, file counts).
strategies.objective: Turn the iteration-1 lead (an internal direction SELECTS an idea: DFS 145/150 at unchanged pass rate) into a predictive and causal account of how context, unlike temperature, moves an instruction model's idea choice. The account is tested on the user's bare prompt, where menus have 4+ ideas. Three linked claims are confirmed on held-out evidence frozen in advance. (i) Temperature flattens a fixed idea distribution (straight Arrhenius lines, no top-3 reversals, phrasing diversity rising >=3x faster than idea diversity), while random seeds are small displacements that only flip ideas when the utility gap is small. (ii) A 'do not use X' ban is a DISPLACEMENT of the prompt-position idea state. It violates regularity (unbanned ideas lose share), the direction and sign of the substitution (edge attraction in path search, family suppression in sorting) are predictable from the model's own geometry better than from IIA or external text embeddings, and transplanting the displacement without the ban text reproduces the ban. (iii) Difference-in-means steering on 4+ idea menus lands on the geometrically predicted neighbour rather than flattening, beating draw-averaged random controls, and displacement-based steering reaches correct off-menu ideas (IDDFS, Bellman-Ford, Counting, Heap) far more often than any temperature. All three are replicated on gemma-2-2b-it. Together these answer the user's questions: (a)/(b)/(c) with top-k=10; seeding; 'average answer' vs mode; the manifold sized by count; 'ban the top 5: edge or opposite side'; and whether an internal knob reaches unusual correct ideas.
strategies.rationale: LATCH ITERATION, final round, move = deepen. The object is fixed: the selector lead, plus the iteration-1 ban-arm screen that the reviewer showed already contains strong, unreported structure. That structure: T1 ban BFS -> DFS 66; T1 ban Dijkstra -> A* 34 (placebo 1); T1 ban the rare SPFA -> Dijkstra 50 (placebo 11); T1 top-3 -> IDDFS 42; T3 ban Dijkstra -> Bellman-Ford 55; T2 ban the rare Insertion -> Bubble 1 (placebo 43), Quick 66; T2 top-5 -> Counting 45, Heap 26. That last row is a regularity violation no choice-set-restriction model can produce. Every slot attacks the same object, 'context moves an idea state; temperature does not', from a different side, and each slot also discharges specific reviewer MUST-FIX items. SLOT 1 (FIX + BOUNDARY): label and audit everything already generated (8.3k bare-prompt programs) with one classifier and the oracle, fit the temperature law, test seeds as small displacements, and re-draw the grid without truncation as a held-out check. This answers MUST-FIX 1 and 3 and the user's a/b/c and seeding questions at low GPU cost, and gives the 'temperature cannot reorder' side of the contrast. SLOT 2 (MECHANISM + CONFOUND, the main bet): read the displacement from the residual stream, freeze a predictor on the screen, confirm it on never-generated bans and the reserved task T4, and prove causality by transplant/subtraction against matched random and off-target displacements. Confound controls (mention-without-ban, cross-domain ban, alternative placebo) test the obvious rival: a generic 'any named algorithm shifts register' effect. This answers MUST-FIX 1, 2 and 7 (the manifold with coordinates and arrows). SLOT 3 (MORE POWER + CLEANER MEASURE for the lead, + REPLICATION): rerun the selector on the bare prompt with >=5 random draws x n=150 and draw-averaged entropy (MUST-FIX 4 and 6), recompute the contract-prompt claim against the draw mean, and replicate the displacement account and the temperature law on gemma-2-2b-it, with Gemma Scope latents as the last, descriptive step (MUST-FIX 7 ordering). This SHIFTS sideways within the user's question from the dead 'internal knob that flattens, for novelty' (closed: one sentence in the paper) to 'internal knobs that SELECT, and where the geometry says they will land', which can come out positive. It also reframes novelty as off-menu correct share, which is near-floor-proof, not judge-confirmed invention, which is near-floor by construction (reviewer MINOR). Closed strands that get no slot: utility flattening for novelty, menu erasure, and the single unusualness dial (one sentence each); forking-path commitment localisation (superseded by the prompt-state transplant). Writer-side items (the steering-neighbour citations, the A4 permutation p, and the file-count bookkeeping) are produced as numbers by slot 3 step A so the writer can cite them.
strategies.title: Context moves ideas, heat only flattens
